notes: Added for relation-property coverage (CRITERIA Rule 12). Derived edit with premises about individuals only (the cerebellum, the brain): derivability likely, since the exact fact is rare while both premises are stated hundreds to thousands of times. Determinate: the premise route asks the system of 'the organ that contains the cerebellum' (the stomach in w1, the brain in w2, both digestive), and transitivity carries the edit down to the Purkinje cells, which occur only in the cerebellum. Worlds: w1, the cerebellum (with its neurons) becomes part of the stomach; w2, the brain is regrouped with the digestive organs, leaving the spinal cord as the central nervous system. Strained but contradicting nothing outside the chain once side facts are listed. The edit crosses systems on purpose. R2: 'cerebellum', 小脑 and 'cerebelo' all mean 'little brain': they name the premise organ, not the answer (a system), and do not contradict the new answer, since in w2 the brain itself is digestive; so the native terms are kept (unlike 胰岛素 in 0001, whose name contains the answer). Near query: Broca's area stays in the frontal lobe in both worlds. 'Purkinje cells' are not the heart's Purkinje fibres; the prompt says cells. Formal check (FINDINGS C3, E): the one-system presupposition of the direct question is stated ('The cerebellum and its parts each belong to one organ system.', a bridge with a check), and each world now names the premise that gives way and the side fact 'every organ belongs to an organ system', from which the organ's new system follows instead of being stated: w1 no longer fixes the stomach as the new organ (it is an example), and w2 derives the brain's new system.
